thread.title: How Dodgers' Edgardo Henriquez Hit 103.3 MPH
thread.title_full: How Dodgers' Edgardo Henriquez Hit 103.3 MPH

author: Sofia Alvarez
title: How Dodgers' Edgardo Henriquez Hit 103.3 MPH
text:
From Catcher to Record-Holder: The Unstoppable Rise of Edgardo Henriquez , the Dodgers’ 103 MPH Flamethrower dodgers reliever Edgardo Henriquez sets a franchise record with a 103.3 mph pitch,capping an incredible journey from catcher to flamethrower.
DENVER – Edgardo Henriquez possesses a rare and formidable gift: a right arm capable of throwing a baseball faster than almost anyone in history. Yet,the 23-year-old phenom for the Los Angeles Dodgers sees his talent not as a gift received, but as a partnership forged through faith and relentless work. “We’ve worked for that,” Henriquez said, frequently enough using the plural to refer to himself. “All the work,the effort,the physics. And God’s reward, most of all.”
That work has culminated in a history-making fastball. On Aug. 16, Henriquez unleashed a 103.3 mph pitch against the San Diego Padres, the fastest recorded by a Dodger sence Statcast began tracking speeds in 2015 and likely the hardest-thrown pitch in the franchise’s storied history. It was a singular moment of dominance that announced the arrival of a truly elite arm in the Dodgers bullpen.
An Unlikely Path From Behind the Plate Henriquez’s journey to the major league mound has been anything but conventional. He was a catcher in his teenage years,a position that demands a diffrent set of skills than those required of a pitcher.But a move to the mound, coupled with a commitment to rigorous training, unlocked a potential that few could have predicted. The transition wasn’t without its hurdles.
He was undergoing Tommy John surgery , a devastating blow for any young pitcher. remarkably, he returned from the elbow reconstruction throwing even harder, his fastball touching 104 mph in the minors last summer.This newfound velocity was so electric that the team moved him permanently to the bullpen,where his career exploded. He ascended four minor league levels in just six months, making his big-league debut late last season.
Another obstacle appeared this spring when a metatarsal injury in his left foot, which he declines to discuss publicly, cost him a spot on the opening day roster. but again, he battled back, striking out 36 batters in 23 2/3 innings at Triple-A Oklahoma City before his latest call-up. The pitcher who returned was a different man.
“He looks much more confident,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He knows his stuff plays hear, so it’s good to see.”
Harnessing the Lightning: More Than Just a Fastball While his record-setting four-seam fastball generates headlines, Henriquez is far from a one-dimensional thrower. His arsenal includes a devastating slider and a mid-90s cutter that has proven nearly unhittable. This secondary weaponry is crucial, as velocity alone is no longer a guarantee of success in the modern game.
“If there isn’t deception, there isn’t ride, [hitters] can catch up if you don’t have something else that they can think about,” noted Chris Forbes, senior director of player development for the Colorado Rockies.
So far, major league hitters are not catching up. In nine innings entering Saturday, Henriquez has allowed just six hits while holding opponents to a .176 batting average. Roberts noted that the coaching staff is working to ensure Henriquez understands that true pitching is an art that goes beyond simply lighting up the radar gun.
His rapid ascent from a teenage catcher to a record-breaking reliever, surviving major surgery and setbacks along the way, is a testament to his resilience. now, with his place in the majors secured, he has one final, unspoken goal.On a team that lacks a defined closer, Henriquez hopes to one day seize that role.
“Whatever God has in store for me. We’ll work wherever and keep going,” he said, before adding with quite ambition, “But yes, I’d like to be a closer.”
